newsitem.title: GERMANY: MAN chief sees another good year in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: MAN chief sees another good year in 1996/97.

text.p: German truck and machinery maker MAN AG should see its business develop positively in the 1996/97 business year and will report a further good result, chairman Klaus Goette said on Tuesday.
Speaking at the company's annual general meeting, Goette said, "positive developments at MAN are continuing and another good result should be made."
He said that if the economy continues to grow, MAN's earnings power will increase in the year which ends June 30.

In the 1995/96 business year MAN reported a group net profit of 330 million marks ($212 million), a 21 percent increase from the year before. Sales climbed to 20.27 billion marks from 18.60 billion marks.
MAN is heavily dependent on wider economic trends and has seen its truck unit, MAN Nutzfahrzeuge AG, hurt by a Europe-wide downturn in the market for heavy trucks.
The company also reported that group sales between July and November climbed two percent from the year ago period to 6.96 billion marks.
Incoming orders, meanwhile, advanced six percent to 9.10 billion marks.
